Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. March 4, 1855 follows a missing Waterhouse note claiming the atlas text should be present. Darwin has searched each page, insists the text is absent from the parcel, and distinguishes maps currently studied from maps and text previously seen at the Athenaeum. A future copy is offered, not received. Carboniferous/Silurian mammals are his hope, not known discoveries. Province without rodents refers to atlas geography, not the tarsal memorandum 1625. Published 1856 edition and later pamphlet possession must not replace the missing contemporary text. No surviving immediate incoming prompt.

Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. July 8, 1855 is supported by endorsement. Darwin asks for an accessible systematic British Lepidoptera guide for his sons, preferring learning from descriptions to mere collecting or pictures. Distinguish the limitations he finds in Stephens, Westwood synopsis, and the magnificent Humphreys/Westwood loan from John Lubbock. The postscript qualifies that Stephens works reasonably for butterflies; book identity in the footnote is probable, not certain. These are initiated questions, not a reply to earlier fossil or tarsal correspondence.
